grade.label: QoR-40: TEAS versus sham, ~24 h
grade.risk_of_bias: Serious: both trials have uncertain patient masking, with additional allocation/missing-data/analysis-plan concerns. All weight comes from Some-concerns results.
grade.inconsistency: No downgrade: the two effects (11.70 and 9.26) are similar with overlapping intervals, I2=0%. With two trials heterogeneity is imprecisely estimated; zero is not proof of homogeneity.
grade.indirectness: No downgrade for the defined adult general-anesthesia TEAS comparison and ~24-hour global recovery endpoint. Applicability remains limited to represented operations and protocols; this is not EA evidence or an opioid-sparing endpoint.
grade.imprecision: Very serious: safeguarded-HK 95% interval crosses both -6.3 and +6.3 points, admitting important harm, no effect and important benefit. Downgrade two levels for decision uncertainty, not simply k=2.
grade.publication_bias: No additional downgrade: too few trials for informative funnel/asymmetry tests. Publication bias cannot be excluded. Other located QoR reports lack compatible statistics or have source holds; available-case synthesis is not a claim of complete recovery evidence.
grade.decision_status: Adopted under user delegation; AI-conducted posthoc assessment

grade.label: QoR-40: TEAS versus usual care, 24 h
grade.risk_of_bias: Serious: Pan (47.1% random-effects weight) is High for recovery-related exclusions and unmasked self-report; Liang has unresolved missingness/masking. One body-level downgrade; source reporting limitations retained.
grade.inconsistency: Serious: effects 2.60 versus 6.30, I2=78.5%, differ relative to the important-benefit benchmark; different procedures and baseline recovery leave variation unexplained.
grade.indirectness: No downgrade for the defined adult general-anesthesia TEAS comparison and ~24-hour global recovery endpoint. Applicability remains limited to represented operations and protocols; this is not EA evidence or an opioid-sparing endpoint.
grade.imprecision: Very serious: safeguarded-HK 95% interval crosses both -6.3 and +6.3 points, admitting important harm, no effect and important benefit. Downgrade two levels for decision uncertainty, not simply k=2.
grade.publication_bias: No additional downgrade: too few trials for informative funnel/asymmetry tests. Publication bias cannot be excluded. Other located QoR reports lack compatible statistics or have source holds; available-case synthesis is not a claim of complete recovery evidence.
grade.decision_status: Adopted under user delegation; AI-conducted posthoc assessment

grade.label: QoR-15: TEAS versus sham, ~24 h
grade.risk_of_bias: Serious: all four subjective results have unresolved patient masking/analysis-plan concerns. Wu has unexplained ITT handling of three missing 24-hour observations; Xing has incompletely explained losses.
grade.inconsistency: Serious: effects range 4.38 to 14.90, I2=80.1%; Wu exceeds the other three. Clinical populations, treatment timing and blocks vary. Leave-one-out analysis identifies influence, not a proven explanatory subgroup.
grade.indirectness: No downgrade for the defined adult general-anesthesia TEAS comparison and ~24-hour global recovery endpoint. Applicability remains limited to represented operations and protocols; this is not EA evidence or an opioid-sparing endpoint.
grade.imprecision: Serious: 95% interval crosses zero and both the 6-point contextual benchmark and historical 8-point benchmark for important benefit. It does not cross -6; downgrade one level. Benchmark choice does not change this judgment.
grade.publication_bias: No additional downgrade: too few trials for informative funnel/asymmetry tests. Publication bias cannot be excluded. Other located QoR reports lack compatible statistics or have source holds; available-case synthesis is not a claim of complete recovery evidence.

rob.d1_rationale: Computer-generated sequence; sequentially numbered opaque sealed envelopes. No baseline pattern suggesting randomization failure was identified.
rob.d2_rationale: Standardized anesthesia/rescue care and masked clinical staff; sensory stimulation before anesthesia could reveal assignment. Three protocol-breach exclusions make assignment-effect analysis uncertain; their details are unavailable. Material trial-context deviations are not established.
rob.d3_rationale: 35/37 TEAS and 36/37 control analyzed. Reasons are only protocol breach, without outcome data or a robustness analysis; outcome-related missingness cannot be excluded.
rob.d4_rationale: Global QoR-40 is self-reported. Current producing muscle twitching versus no current may reveal assignment despite the masking claim and midazolam premedication. No masking-success test establishes whether awareness influenced reporting.
rob.d5_rationale: The publication identifies 24-hour global QoR-40 as primary, but a prospective exact-result analysis plan was not independently verified. No direct evidence of selection among measurements or analyses was found.
rob.overall_rationale: Residual uncertainty requires Some concerns. Multiple concerns were considered jointly, not mechanically counted; available evidence does not establish likely material bias warranting High.

rob.d1_rationale: Computer sequence and nurse-mediated assignment are reported; a tamper-resistant concealment mechanism is not described.
rob.d2_rationale: Standardized care, masked clinical personnel and all 60 participants analyzed as assigned. No trial-context departures affecting recovery are reported; awareness alone is not such a departure.
rob.d3_rationale: Complete datasets are explicitly reported for all 60 randomized participants; 30 per arm.
rob.d4_rationale: Patient-reported QoR-40 with 12-15 mA preanesthetic twitching versus no current. Identical electrodes and a masked interviewer do not demonstrate patient masking; influence on reporting remains possible rather than proven.
rob.d5_rationale: POD1/POD2 global QoR named in methods; no verified prospective analysis plan. Published repeated-measures/adjusted P values are not the unadjusted endpoint contrast used here, and are not substituted for its calculated uncertainty.
rob.overall_rationale: Residual uncertainty requires Some concerns. Multiple concerns were considered jointly, not mechanically counted; available evidence does not establish likely material bias warranting High.

rob.comparison: TEAS vs no stimulation; dummy electrodes not documented
rob.d1_rationale: Independent computer-generated sequence and identical sealed envelopes support probably concealed allocation. No imbalance pattern suggesting failure was identified.
rob.d2_rationale: Anesthetist and follow-up investigator are masked. Dummy electrodes and patient masking are not established, and five randomized patients are removed. No documented material differential cointervention, but trial-context deviation information is incomplete.
rob.d3_rationale: Flowchart distinguishes 80 screened from 75 randomized (37/38), with 35/35 analyzed. Two procedural/blood-sampling losses and three changed surgeries do not establish ignorable missing QoR outcomes.
rob.d4_rationale: Validated patient-reported QoR-40. No-current usual-care description does not document a credible sham; patient awareness at assessment is unclear. Interviewer masking cannot resolve this, so Some concerns rather than assuming either successful masking or definite influence.
rob.d5_rationale: 24/48-hour total QoR is described, but no independently verified prospective exact-result analysis plan. No direct evidence of result selection.
rob.overall_rationale: Residual uncertainty requires Some concerns. Multiple concerns were considered jointly, not mechanically counted; available evidence does not establish likely material bias warranting High.

rob.d1_rationale: Random-number tables reported; allocation concealment is not described sufficiently.
rob.d2_rationale: No sham and the practitioner knows assignment. Exclusions for non-protocol analgesia/PCIA make assignment-effect analysis problematic. Reasons for these departures are unclear, so their trial-context origin is not asserted; resulting outcome-related missingness is assessed in D3.
rob.d3_rationale: 120 enrolled, 105 analyzed. Exclusions include analgesics outside plan, PCIA, changed surgery and bleeding, all potentially related to recovery. Informative missingness is likely; final table denominators 52/53 are retained without claiming full ITT.
rob.d4_rationale: Self-reported global QoR after preoperative and PACU stimulation versus no TEAS. Patients probably know allocation and awareness is likely to influence subjective reporting. A masked pain-assessment nurse does not mask the patient QoR assessor.
rob.d5_rationale: 24-hour QoR-40 identified as a main index, but prospective exact-result plan not independently verified. No direct evidence of selecting this global score among alternate results.
rob.overall_rationale: Likely informative missingness and awareness-related reporting bias (D3/D4).

rob.comparison: TEAS vs no-current electrodes; TAP block in both arms
rob.d1_rationale: Independent SPSS sequence, sealed envelopes and assignment revealed only at first intervention support probably concealed allocation.
rob.d2_rationale: Common anesthesia, TAP block and analgesia; practitioner unmasked but otherwise masking reported and no material trial-context departures documented. One withdrawal per arm, with nearly all assigned participants assessed.
rob.d3_rationale: 72/74 analyzed (36/37 each). Two personal-reason withdrawals, no recovery-related pattern documented; nearly all data available. This is a contextual judgment, not a universal attrition cutoff.
rob.d4_rationale: QoR-15 is self-reported. Acupuncture-naive patients were told stimulation might not be felt, supporting masking, but vibration at 6-15 mA over three sessions versus a disabled device could still reveal allocation. Reporting influence remains uncertain.
rob.d5_rationale: Registration is reported as preceding recruitment and QoR is named in published methods, but prospective exact-result/timepoint/analysis specification has not been independently verified.
rob.overall_rationale: Residual uncertainty requires Some concerns. Multiple concerns were considered jointly, not mechanically counted; available evidence does not establish likely material bias warranting High.

rob.comparison: PACU TEAS vs no-current electrodes; paravertebral block in both arms
rob.d1_rationale: Independent computer sequence at PACU arrival. Serial-number correspondence is described but the concealment mechanism is insufficiently explicit.
rob.d2_rationale: Same anesthesia/block and stated rescue policy. Practitioner awareness does not itself establish a deviation, and no trial-context departures are documented. The report claims assignment-based ITT; unexplained missing-data handling is evaluated in D3.
rob.d3_rationale: PDF p4 flowchart: 50/50 randomized, 48/49 completed, 50/50 included in ITT. Three early-discharge patients lack 24-hour contact; handling/imputation is not explained. Recovery-dependent missingness is plausible, but likely direction/materiality cannot be established. N=100 is reported analysis N, not 100 observed scores.
rob.d4_rationale: PACU residual anesthesia may protect masking, but the authors acknowledge sensory differences as patients awaken. Self-reported 24-hour QoR could be influenced; no demonstrated masking success. This differs from the pre-intervention opioid assessment.
rob.d5_rationale: 24-hour QoR-15 is a named secondary outcome; no independently verified prospective exact-result analysis plan. No direct evidence that the reported total was selected from multiple results.
rob.overall_rationale: Residual uncertainty requires Some concerns. Multiple concerns were considered jointly, not mechanically counted; available evidence does not establish likely material bias warranting High.

rob.comparison: NTG vs NG: TEAS+TAP block vs sham+TAP block; G arm excluded
rob.d1_rationale: Computer sequence and sealed code delivered to an independent nurse. Printed 1:1:1:1 ratio conflicts with the three-arm trial but is treated as a reporting error, not proof of nonrandom allocation.
rob.d2_rationale: NTG versus NG preserves TAP block in both arms; G is not used. Masked clinical team and no documented departures affecting assignment effect.
rob.d3_rationale: 29/30 per relevant arm analyzed after one loss to follow-up each. Exact reasons and outcome availability at POD1 versus later follow-up are unspecified; possible outcome-related missingness cannot be excluded.
rob.d4_rationale: Self-reported QoR. Authors explicitly acknowledge possible unblinding because TEAS began before anesthesia; hiding the stimulator and masking data collectors do not establish patient masking. Influence is possible, not established as likely.
rob.d5_rationale: Published primary QoR at POD1/3/7, without independent verification of a prospective exact-result analysis plan. This review fixes POD1 rather than selecting the largest later contrast.
rob.overall_rationale: Residual uncertainty requires Some concerns. Multiple concerns were considered jointly, not mechanically counted; available evidence does not establish likely material bias warranting High.

rob.d1_rationale: Computer sequence, sequential opaque sealed envelopes and an independent assistant uninvolved in recruitment/outcomes.
rob.d2_rationale: Scripted neutral interaction, common anesthesia/analgesia, no documented trial-context departures. 97/100 assigned participants analyzed; no substantial assignment-analysis error established.
rob.d3_rationale: Two TEAS and one sham withdrawals (48/50 and 49/50 assessed). Nearly all data and no documented recovery-related pattern. No imputation is claimed.
rob.d4_rationale: Self-reported QoR after PACU active current versus no current. Scripted interaction supports masking but preoperative current calibration and sensory differences could reveal assignment; influence on reporting remains uncertain.
rob.d5_rationale: POD1 global QoR is the sample-size target and all three days are reported, but prospective exact-result analysis specification is unverified. The contradictory POD3 P value is a separate held timepoint, not a reason to replace the POD1 data.
rob.overall_rationale: Residual uncertainty requires Some concerns. Multiple concerns were considered jointly, not mechanically counted; available evidence does not establish likely material bias warranting High.
